predecessor_evidence.interpretation: V22's persistent learned screen is broadly valuable, but the primary-empty loop remains instruction-identical to V17 and therefore only ties it. V23 makes one source-general loop-state improvement: keep the primary pointer authoritative and remove one integer cursor update from every primary-empty 64-candidate group. No failing row, width, topology, outcome, pattern, density threshold, or corpus member is removed or routed around.

declared_design.summary: Retain V22's complete persistent learned-column graph. Before learning, represent the primary-only 64-candidate loop with X15 as the authoritative primary-column pointer and X13 as its inclusive final-wide pointer. Advance only X15 after a primary-empty group. Reconstruct X5 exactly from X15, the haystack base, and the sealed primary offset at every exit from pointer-only state before any existing V22 consumer executes.
declared_design.scope: All admitted exact byte literals of widths 6 through 32 on AArch64 ASIMD. No pattern, topology, width, corpus, density, outcome, runtime-result, or invocation-count dispatch is permitted.

unchanged_prefix: V22 primary literal broadcast and every static literal broadcast
V22 window validation and wide/narrow/tail eligibility checks
pointer_wide_setup: Retain X7 equal to end_index minus 63.
Set X13 to haystack plus X7 plus the authenticated primary offset; X13 is the inclusive primary-column pointer for the last valid 64-candidate group.
X15 remains haystack plus the current candidate base plus the authenticated primary offset.
X5 is authoritative on entry to the first primary-wide group.
primary_empty_advance: After the four primary masks prove empty, increment X15 by 64 and do not update X5.
Compare X15 directly with X13 and continue the primary-wide loop while X15 is at most X13.
On wide exhaustion, reconstruct X5 as X15 minus haystack minus primary_offset before entering unchanged V22 narrow setup.
The optimization removes exactly one X5 add per primary-empty 64-candidate group; it adds no load, vector instruction, data-dependent threshold, or corpus-specific branch.
primary_hit_exit: Before entering V22's secondary/static filtering graph, reconstruct X5 as X15 minus haystack minus primary_offset.
Every secondary-only, remaining-static, learned-discovery, saved-queue, result-publication, narrow, and tail consumer therefore observes the unchanged V22 X5/X15 contract.
Any pre-learning static-empty edge that returns to primary-wide advance retains X15 as the current primary pointer; the advance makes X5 stale only after incrementing X15.
X13 remains the final-wide pointer across all pre-learning paths that can return to pointer-wide advance.
The first permitted X13 clobber is at wide_learn_select, is dominated by mandatory X5 reconstruction, and has no successor edge back to pre-learning pointer-wide advance.
unchanged_v22_graph: Secondary-only mode and its primary recheck
First false-survivor exact confirmation and mismatch discovery
Q24 learned byte, Q25 learned offset, and X11 learned state
Persistent learned-wide screening and empty advance
Four-mask ordered exact queue and source-order behavior
All output publication and ABI paths
unchanged_suffix: V17 scalar tail and exact-return ABI
V17, V19, V20, V21, and V22 emitted images
All non-V23 backend policies and wire formats

pointer_only_prelearning_state: X15 = current primary-column pointer and is authoritative
X13 = inclusive final valid primary-column pointer
X5 may lag X15 only between a primary-empty advance and the mandatory reconstruction at a pointer-loop exit
the primary offset is sealed in the search manifest and immediate instruction stream
reconstruction: if primary_offset is nonzero, X5 = X5 minus primary_offset
reconstruction occurs before every branch from pointer-only state to existing V22 code
persistent_learned_state: Identical to V22: X11 is one outside the temporary four-entry queue, Q24 is the learned literal byte, and Q25 is the learned offset
V23 pointer-only X13 state is dead once learning begins; V22 may reuse X13 normally
register_contract.scratch: No new architectural register is introduced. X13 replaces its pre-learning scratch role only while a path can return to primary-wide advance.

requirements: V23 adds no instruction to emitted V17, V19, V20, V21, or V22 images.
The primary-empty steady-state loop has one fewer integer instruction per 64 candidates than V22.
No pointer-wide exit reaches V22 code with stale X5.
X13 is not overwritten on any pre-learning path that can return to pointer-wide advance.

V22's persistent learned graph retains the same decoded non-relocation instruction/register sequence and control-flow semantics; authenticated PC-relative branch displacements may be regenerated because V23 changes surrounding instruction positions.
No new literal column, density counter, runtime threshold, memory spill, or pattern dispatch is emitted.
All direct branches and relocations remain within authenticated AArch64 encodings.

required: Emitter/template byte-for-byte agreement and whole-image audit acceptance.
Version 36, magic 0x24, AOT, audit, runtime allowlist, mutation, and reseal rejection coverage.
All supported search output contracts emit, audit, serialize, adopt, and execute or explicitly reject V23 consistently.

Mechanical byte identity for every previously supported backend/image, including all V1 through V22 ASIMD and SVE/SVE2 variants, against implementation commit acffd515255e94c6b9fc0163f5f9992989363e9f.
Decoded proof of X13 final-pointer initialization for both zero and nonzero primary offsets.
Decoded control-flow proof that every pointer-wide exit reconstructs X5 before a pre-existing V22 consumer and that every pointer-wide backedge preserves X13.
Decoded dominator proof that wide_learn_select is the first allowed X13 clobber, is reached only after X5 reconstruction, and has no successor capable of reaching pre-learning pointer-wide advance.
Decoded proof that the primary-empty steady state removes exactly the X5 add and changes its bound comparison from X5/X7 to X15/X13.
Mutation rejection for X13 initialization, pointer advance, pointer comparison, and both reconstruction operands.
Primary-empty transitions across at least three consecutive 64-candidate groups followed by narrow, tail, no-match, and exact-match exits.
Primary-hit/pair-empty secondary-only transitions and every remaining-static-empty return to pointer-wide advance.
V22 learned-empty, learned-nonempty same-block/later-block/later-group, and persistent pair-empty cases remain exact.
Widths 6 through 32 cover zero and nonzero primary offsets plus every mismatch offset outside the authenticated static offsets.
Windows cover wide-to-narrow and narrow-to-tail boundaries at every residue modulo 16.
Randomized windows and left/right guard-page native execution on the EC2 c9g host.

fresh_performance_gate.method: Paired portable/V17/V23; 12 repetitions; all 6 execution orders; approximately 4 ms target per measurement; semantic equality checked before and during timing.

topologies.unique: byte i is 33 + ((17*i) mod 64), unique for the admitted width
topologies.clustered-repeat: fill with '~' and replace the first five bytes with 'A3mQz'
topologies.spaced-repeat: fill with 'x' and write M/N/O/P/R at 0, width/4, width/2, 3*width/4, and width-1 in that order
topologies.seeded-mixed: deterministic xorshift64 stream mapped to a fixed 16-byte printable alphabet, independently seeded by width

scenarios: random-absent with seed 0x9e3779b97f4a7c15 mixed with topology and width
dense-near-miss-first-unfiltered using the first offset outside the five authenticated offsets
dense-near-miss-last-unfiltered using the last offset outside the five authenticated offsets
sparse-singleton-unfiltered injected every 257 bytes into an avoiding-byte background

strict_acceptance.artifact_pairs: one frozen V17/V23 pair per topology and width
